concepts.name: Electric Charge
concepts.description: Charge is a property of matter. Like charges repel and unlike charges attract. It is measured in coulombs (C); the electron carries 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C.
objectives: State the SI unit of charge
Relate charge to number of electrons

concepts.name: Electric Current
concepts.description: Current is the rate of flow of charge, I = Q/t, measured in amperes. Conventional current is taken from the positive to the negative terminal.
objectives: Define current and use I = Q/t
Explain how an ammeter is connected

concepts.name: Electric Circuit
concepts.description: A circuit is a closed conducting path with a source. Current flows only when the path is complete.
objectives: Give the direction of conventional current

concepts.name: Potential Difference
concepts.description: Potential difference is the work done per unit charge, V = W/Q, measured in volts. A voltmeter is connected in parallel.
objectives: Explain how a voltmeter is connected

concepts.name: Ohm’s Law
concepts.description: At constant temperature the current through a conductor is proportional to the potential difference across it: V = IR.
objectives: Predict how current changes with V or R

concepts.name: Resistance
concepts.description: Resistance is the opposition a conductor offers to current, R = V/I, measured in ohms.
objectives: Calculate R from V and I

concepts.name: Factors Affecting Resistance
concepts.description: R = ρL/A. Resistance grows with length and falls with cross-sectional area; it also depends on material and temperature.

concepts.name: Series Combination
concepts.description: In series the same current flows through every resistor, the voltages add, and Rs = R1 + R2 + R3.

concepts.name: Parallel Combination
concepts.description: In parallel each branch has the same voltage, currents add, and 1/Rp = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + … so Rp is smaller than any branch.

concepts.name: Heating Effect of Current
concepts.description: A current in a resistor produces heat, H = I²Rt (Joule’s law).
objectives: Predict how heat scales with I

concepts.name: Electric Power
concepts.description: Power is the rate of energy transfer, P = VI = I²R = V²/R, measured in watts.
objectives: Choose between P = I²R and V²/R

concepts.name: Electrical Energy
concepts.description: Energy used is E = P×t. The commercial unit is the kilowatt-hour: 1 kWh = 3.6×10⁶ J.

questions.q: Two small balls both carry negative charge and are brought close together. They…
questions.ex: Like charges repel. Only unlike charges attract.

questions.q: A glass rod rubbed with silk becomes positively charged. This is because the glass rod…
questions.ex: Only electrons move between the solids. Losing electrons leaves more protons than electrons, so the rod is positive.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of electric charge?
questions.ex: Charge is measured in coulombs. The ampere is a coulomb per second.

questions.q: What is the charge, in coulombs, on 1000 electrons? (e = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C; enter like 1.6e-16)
Electric current is best defined as…
o: Rate of flow of electric charge
Opposition to the flow of charge
questions.ex: I = Q/t: charge per second. Energy per unit charge is potential difference.

questions.q: 12 C of charge passes a point in 4 s. What is the current in amperes?
An ammeter before a bulb reads 0.5 A. What does an identical ammeter placed after the bulb read?
questions.ex: Charge is not used up. The same current leaves the bulb; the electrical energy is what is transferred.

questions.q: Why must an ammeter be connected in series with the component being measured?
questions.ex: It has to carry the whole current of that branch, so it sits in the path of the current.

questions.q: Potential difference between two points is…
questions.ex: V = W/Q, in joules per coulomb (volts).

questions.q: 36 J of work is done moving 6 C between two points. What is the potential difference in volts?
How is a voltmeter connected to measure the potential difference across a bulb?
o: In parallel with the battery only
questions.ex: A voltmeter has very high resistance and sits across the component.

questions.q: What must be true for a current to flow in a circuit?
questions.ex: Charge needs a closed loop with a source.

questions.q: Outside the cell, conventional current flows…
o: From the positive terminal to the negative terminal
From the negative terminal to the positive terminal
questions.ex: By convention current runs positive to negative externally; electrons drift the opposite way.

questions.q: What happens to the current in a series circuit when the switch is opened? Say why.
questions.ex: Opening the switch breaks the closed path, so the current falls to zero everywhere in the series loop.

questions.q: Which expression is Ohm’s law?
questions.ex: V = IR, or I = V/R.

questions.q: A 12 V supply is across a 4 Ω resistor. What current flows, in amperes?
The voltage across a resistor stays constant while its resistance increases. The current…
questions.ex: I = V/R. With V fixed, a larger R gives a smaller I.

questions.q: A 10 V supply is connected across a resistor. The resistor is changed from 2 Ω to 5 Ω. What happens to the current?
o: It decreases from 5 A to 2 A
It increases from 2 A to 5 A
questions.ex: I = V/R. At 2 Ω the current is 5 A; at 5 Ω it is 2 A, so more resistance means less current.

questions.q: A conductor carries 0.5 A at 2 V. At the same temperature, what current flows at 6 V (in amperes)?
questions.ex: R = 2/0.5 = 4 Ω. I = 6/4 = 1.5 A. Current is proportional to V.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of resistance?
questions.ex: One ohm is one volt per ampere.

questions.q: A component has 9 V across it and carries 0.3 A. What is its resistance in ohms?
The length of a uniform wire is doubled. Its resistance…
questions.ex: R = ρL/A is proportional to L.

questions.q: The cross-sectional area of a wire is doubled, length unchanged. Its resistance…
questions.ex: R is inversely proportional to A.

questions.q: A wire has resistance 8 Ω. It is replaced by one of the same material with twice the length and twice the cross-sectional area. What is the new resistance in ohms?
questions.ex: Doubling L doubles R and doubling A halves it, so R stays 8 Ω.

questions.q: Resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 5 Ω are in series. What is the equivalent resistance in ohms?
Three bulbs are connected in series. The current through each bulb is…
questions.ex: There is only one path, so the current is the same everywhere in a series loop.

questions.q: A 6 V battery is connected across 2 Ω and 4 Ω resistors in series. What is the current in amperes?
questions.ex: Rs = 6 Ω, so I = 6/6 = 1 A.

questions.q: Resistors connected in parallel across a battery all have…
questions.ex: Each branch is connected directly across the same two points.

questions.q: 6 Ω and 3 Ω resistors are in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance in ohms?
Compared with the smallest resistor in a parallel group, the equivalent resistance is…
questions.ex: Every extra branch gives the current another path, so the total resistance drops below the smallest branch.

questions.q: Which device mainly uses the heating effect of current?
questions.ex: A heater’s element converts electrical energy to heat as current passes through its resistance.

questions.q: A 5 Ω resistor carries 2 A for 10 s. How much heat is produced in joules?
The current in a resistor is doubled for the same time. The heat produced…
questions.ex: H = I²Rt, so doubling I multiplies the heat by 4.

questions.q: Which expression gives electric power?
questions.ex: P = VI. Combined with V = IR it gives I²R and V²/R.

questions.q: An appliance runs on 220 V and draws 5 A. What is its power in watts?
A 60 W lamp runs on 120 V. What current does it draw, in amperes?
A 2 kW heater runs for 3 hours. How much energy is used, in kWh?
questions.ex: E = P × t = 2 × 3 = 6 kWh.

questions.q: 1 kilowatt-hour equals…
A 40 W and a 100 W bulb are rated for the same voltage. Which has the greater resistance?
questions.ex: R = V²/P. For the same V, a smaller P means a larger R.
